newsitem.title: UK: Fitch rates Citicorp mortgage certs AAA.
newsitem.headline: Fitch rates Citicorp mortgage certs AAA.

text.p: Fitch Investors Service said on Thursday it rated AAA Citicorp Mortgage Securities Inc.'s (CMSI) $189 million mortgage pass-through certificates, series 1996-1, class A.
It said in a statement it also rated the $4.0 million class M certificates AA, the $2.5 million class B-1 A and the $2.0 million class B-2 BBB.

The AAA'rating on class A senior certificates reflects the subordination of the 2.00% class M, the 1.25% class B-1, the 1.00% class B-2 and the 1.25% unoffered class B certificates. Fitch believes the amount of credit enhancement will be sufficient to cover credit losses, including limited bankruptcy, fraud and special hazard losses.

The rating also reflects the high quality of the underlying collateral, the integrity of the legal and financial structures and the servicing capabilities of affiliate Citicorp Mortgage, Inc. (CMI). The mortgage pool consists of recently originated, conventional, 20- to 30-year fixed-rate mortgage loans secured by one- to four-family residential properties located primarily in California (27.20%), New York (15.57%) and New Jersey (6.54%).

The weighted average original loan to value ratio (LTV) of the pool is approximately 75.57%. Loans originated under a limited loan documentation program account for approximately 1.38% of the pool, cash-out refinance loans 5.17%, one- to four-family detached properties 97.46% and jumbo loans (balances greater than $300,000) 50.99%.

The weighted average coupon of the loans is 8.26% and the weighted average remaining term is 355 months. The mortgage loans were originated or acquired by CMI and in turn sold to CMSI. CMSI, a special purpose corporation, deposited the loans into the trust, which then issued the certificates. The Bank of New York will serve as trustee. For federal income tax purposes, two real estate mortgage investment conduits will be made with respect to the trust fund.
